words.gloss: by the taking of a debt

hindi: दिए हुए का न देना ऋण लेने के द्वारा समझाया गया।
english: Non-giving of what was given has been explained by the taking of a debt.
notes: dattasya-apradānam is read literally as 'non-giving of what was given' (the withholding of a gift); the sense of the heading (non-delivery of a promised gift or cancelling of a gift) is not decided here. ṛṇa-ādāna is literally 'taking (up) of a debt'; the alternative that it names the recovery of a debt is not excluded.

hindi: दिया हुआ व्यवहार के योग्य नहीं है; एक स्थान पर पश्चात्ताप होने पर स्थित रहे।
english: What is given is not to be dealt with (as a legal matter); it would stand in one case of regret.
notes: Obscure sentence; rendered literally. avyavahārya may mean 'not actionable at law'. ekatra could be 'in one (case)' or 'in one place'; the subject of varteta (the gift, or the rule) is not stated. Low confidence.

hindi: सब धन, पुत्र-पत्नी या स्वयं को देकर पश्चात्ताप करने वाले को दे।
english: Having given all property, sons and wife, or himself, [one] should give to the regretful one.
notes: Obscure: anuśayinaḥ may be genitive sg. (of the regretful one, used for the recipient), accusative pl., or ablative sg.; who gives to whom (and what) is not stated. Rendered literally. Low confidence.

hindi: धर्म के लिए दान असाधु कर्मों में या हानिकारक कर्मों में, अर्थ के लिए दान उपकार न करने वालों को या अपकार करने वालों को, और काम के लिए दान अयोग्यों को।
english: A gift for dharma [made] in improper actions or in injurious ones, a gift for wealth [made] to non-benefactors or to wrongdoers, and a gift for desire [made] to the unworthy.
notes: Verbless list of the kinds of gift; what follows from them is not stated here. In 'asādhuṣu karmasu ca aupaghātikeṣu vā' both ca and vā occur; ca is glossed 'also' and the 'or' of vā is rendered, the exact connection is uncertain. The compounds dharma-dāna etc. could also be 'gift as dharma'.

hindi: और जिस प्रकार दाता और प्रतिग्रहीता क्षतिग्रस्त न हों, उस प्रकार कुशल पश्चात्ताप का निर्धारण करें।
english: And so that neither the giver nor the receiver would be harmed, the skilled should so arrange the regret.
notes: anuśaya is rendered 'regret' as in units 2-3; here it may denote the cancellation (rescission) of a gift because of regret.

words.gram: m. gen. sg., pres. part. prati-√grah
m. gen. sg., pres. part. pra-√yam

hindi: दण्ड के भय से, आक्रोश के भय से या अनर्थ के भय से दिए गए भय-दान को लेने वाले का चोरी का दण्ड, और देने वाले का।
english: A fear-gift [made] from fear of punishment, from fear of abuse, or from fear of loss: for one who accepts [it] the penalty for theft [is due], and for one who gives [it] as well.
notes: Verbless; the genitives are taken as 'for the one who accepts' and 'for the one who gives'. 'and for one who gives' repeats steya-daṇḍaḥ by ellipsis. anartha = loss (अनर्थ), as in the glossary; ākrośa = abuse, reviling.

hindi: रोष का दान दूसरों की हिंसा में, और राजाओं के ऊपर दर्प का दान।
english: A gift of anger [made] in injuring others, and a gift of pride [made] over kings.
notes: Verbless, continuing the list of units 4 and 6. roṣa = anger (not kopa). upari rājñām could be 'against kings' or 'above kings'; rendered 'over'. Low-medium sense; confidence medium.

hindi: वहाँ सर्वोच्च दण्ड।
english: There, the highest penalty [is due].
notes: tatra 'there' is taken as 'in that matter' (the gifts of fear, anger and pride in units 6-7); the exact reference is not fixed.

hindi: प्रातिभाव्य, दण्ड और शुल्क का शेष, पासों से सम्बन्धित और सौरिक, अनिच्छुक नहीं, पुत्र या दायाद या रिक्थ लेने वाला दे। यह दिए हुए का अनपाकर्म है।
english: Suretyship, the remainder of a fine and toll, what pertains to dice, and the saurika: a son, or an heir, or the taker of the inheritance, not unwilling, should give [them]. Such is the non-withdrawal of what was given.
notes: na-akāmaḥ is rendered literally 'not unwilling'; the sense may be 'should not give if unwilling', i.e. he pays only willingly. saurika is obscure (kept untranslated, as in the glossary); ākṣika taken as 'pertaining to dice', the object (debt) is not stated. anapākarma = non-withdrawal (of a gift), the label closing the section; its iti is glossed 'closing particle'.

hindi: किन्तु अस्वामी का विक्रय: खोए और चुराए हुए को पाकर स्वामी धर्मस्थ के द्वारा पकड़वाए।
english: But as to sale by a non-owner: the owner, having found what is lost and stolen, should cause [it] to be seized through the dharmastha.
notes: grāhayet is rendered literally 'cause to be seized' (glossary); the sense (have it held, arrested or claimed) is not decided. dharmastha kept as a title. naṣṭa-apahṛta could be 'lost or stolen'.

words.gloss: in the lapse of place and time

hindi: अथवा देश और काल का अतिक्रमण होने पर स्वयं लेकर प्रस्तुत करे।
english: Or, when place and time have been exceeded, having taken [it] himself, [he] should present [it].
notes: Obscure. The subject of upaharet (owner or dharmastha) and the object are not stated. atipatti = passing beyond, lapse; 'place and time' may refer to limits of locality and period for the claim. Low-medium confidence.

hindi: और धर्मस्थ स्वामी से पूछताछ करे: “तुम्हारे द्वारा कहाँ से प्राप्त किया गया?”
english: And the dharmastha should question the owner: “From where [was it] obtained by you?”
notes: te may be instrumental (by you) or genitive (your). The closing iti is carried by the quotation marks only (glossary).

hindi: यदि वह आचार का क्रम दिखाए, विक्रेता को नहीं, उस द्रव्य के समर्पण से छूट जाए।
english: If he should show the sequence of practice, but not the seller, he would be released by the giving over of that property.
notes: ācāra-krama is rendered literally; it is commonly understood as the sequence of transfers by which he obtained the thing (not decided here). atisarga = giving over, handing over. The sentence is elliptical (darśayeta understood with na vikretāram).

hindi: यदि विक्रेता दिखाई दे, मूल्य और चोरी का दण्ड दे।
english: If the seller is seen, [he] should give the price and the penalty for theft.
notes: The subject of dadyāt is taken to be the seller. dṛśyeta 'is seen' = is found.

words.gloss: up to the loss of the apasāra

hindi: यदि वह अपसार को प्राप्त करे, अपसार के क्षय तक हट जाए।
english: If he should reach the apasāra, [he] should move away up to the loss of the apasāra.
notes: apasāra is kept untranslated (glossary 4.6/4.8: the person or thing pointed to as source; sense not settled); the sentence is obscure and the subject of apasaret is not stated. The sandhi d in adhigacched / apasared is regular. ā with the ablative = 'up to'.

hindi: क्षय होने पर मूल्य और चोरी का दण्ड दे।
english: On loss, [he] should give the price and the penalty for theft.
notes: Continues unit 15; 'loss' (kṣaya) is of the apasāra, if that reading holds. Subject not stated.

hindi: और खोने वाला अपना प्रमाण प्रस्तुत करके खोए और लौटाए हुए को पाए।
english: And the loser, having furnished his own means of proof, would obtain what was lost and brought back.
notes: nāṣṭika is taken as 'the one who has lost' (naṣṭa + -ika). sva-karaṇa = means of proof (glossary 4.1). kṛtvā is literally 'having made'; 'furnished' / प्रस्तुत करके renders the idiom, medium confidence. pratyāhṛta = brought back, recovered.

words.gloss: in the absence of own means of proof

hindi: अपने प्रमाण के अभाव में पञ्च-बन्ध दण्ड।
english: In the absence of his own means of proof, the penalty [is] pañca-bandha.
notes: pañca-bandha is obscure and is kept untranslated (literally 'five-bond'); some understand it as a penalty of one-fifth, but this is not decided here.

hindi: और वह द्रव्य राजधर्म्य हो।
english: And that property would be rāja-dharmya (of the king's dharma).
notes: rāja-dharmya taken literally as 'relating to the king's dharma'; probably 'due to the king', but the sense is not decided here.

words.gram: m. gen. sg., pres. part. ut-√kṛṣ

hindi: खोए और चुराए हुए को बिना बताए उठाने वाले स्वामी को प्रथम साहस-दण्ड।
english: For the owner who takes up what is lost and stolen without reporting [it]: the first fine for rashness.
notes: utkarṣataḥ taken as present participle of ut-√kṛṣ 'drawing up, taking up' agreeing with svāminaḥ; the exact sense of the act is not decided. The genitive is rendered 'for the owner'.

hindi: शुल्क-स्थान पर खोया, चुराया और उत्पन्न हुआ ठहरा रहे।
english: At the toll-station, what is lost, stolen and arisen should remain.
notes: utpanna 'arisen' (perhaps 'turned up') is rendered literally. The listed things may be distinct items, not three descriptions of one.

words.gloss: by his own means of proof

hindi: तीन पक्ष के बाद अनभिसार को राजा ले, या स्वामी अपने प्रमाण से।
english: After three fortnights the king may take the unclaimed [thing], or the owner [may take it] by his own means of proof.
notes: anabhisāra is literally 'not approached' (no one has come for it); abhisāra here is not the 8.5 'reinforcement'. Kept as the Sanskrit term in Hindi.

hindi: द्विपद रूप का निष्क्रय पाँच पण वाला दे, एक खुर वाले का चार पण वाला, गाय-भैंस का दो पण वाला, छोटे पशुओं का चौथाई वाला।
english: [He] should give a redemption price of five paṇas for a two-footed form, [one] of four paṇas for a one-hoofed [animal], [one] of two paṇas for a cow-and-buffalo, [one] of a quarter for small animals.
notes: dvipada-rūpa is rendered literally ('two-footed form'); rūpa may rather be a coin or 'figure' (the sense 'human being' is possible), not decided. pādika = of a quarter (of a paṇa, understood). The glossary keeps paṇa as a unit name.

words.gloss: of gems, valuables, trifling things and raw materials

hindi: रत्न, बहुमूल्य, तुच्छ और कुप्य के विषय में सौ में पाँच दे।
english: For gems, valuables, trifling [things] and raw materials, [he] should give five in a hundred.
notes: pañcakaṃ śataṃ is read as 'five (per) hundred'; the sense of the quantity (of value) is not stated. phalgu = trifling (literally 'weak, inferior'); sāra = valuables (glossary 12.1); kupya = raw materials.

words.gloss: carried off by the enemy's troops and forest tribes

hindi: किन्तु शत्रु की सेना और वन की जातियों द्वारा हरे गए को वापस लाकर राजा यथास्व दे।
english: But what has been carried off by the enemy's troops and forest tribes, the king, having brought [it] back, should give according to each one's own.
notes: Following the glossary (4.12, 8.4): para-cakra = the enemy's troops, aṭavī = forest tribes. yathā-svam is read as 'to each according to what is his own'.

words.gram: n. acc. sg., pres. part. pass. a-√vid

hindi: चोरों द्वारा हरे गए और न मिलने वाले को अपने द्रव्यों से दे, या वापस लाने में असमर्थ।
english: What was carried off by thieves and is not to be found, [he] should give from his own property, or [he who is] unable to bring [it] back.
notes: Elliptical; the subject (the king or the officer concerned) is not stated, and the final phrase may mean 'or if he is unable to bring it back'. avidyamāna literally 'not existing'.

hindi: स्वयं-ग्रह से लिए गए को वापस लाकर दे, या उसका निष्क्रय।
english: Having brought back what was taken by self-seizure, [he] should give [it], or its redemption price.
notes: svayam-grāha is rendered literally 'seizure by oneself'; its exact sense (seizure by the claimant himself, or by an officer) is not decided. The giver is not stated.

words.gloss: from the property of gods, Brahmins and ascetics

hindi: अथवा दूसरे देश से पराक्रम द्वारा लाए गए को राजा के निर्देश के अनुसार भोगे, आर्य-प्राणों और देव, ब्राह्मण, तपस्वियों के द्रव्यों को छोड़कर। यह अस्वामी का विक्रय है।
english: Or what has been brought from another territory by valour, [he] should enjoy as directed by the king, except for ārya lives and the property of gods, Brahmins and ascetics. Such is the sale by a non-owner.
notes: ārya-prāṇa is literal ('ārya lives'); it may mean ārya persons. 'Valour' for vikrama (alternative 'force'). The closing 'ity asvāmi-vikrayaḥ' follows the glossary (3.7): 'Such is X', iti glossed 'closing particle'.

words.gloss: of those whose regions are destroyed

hindi: किन्तु स्व और स्वामी का सम्बन्ध: जिनके देश नष्ट हो गए हैं उनके द्रव्यों के भोग की निरन्तरता यथास्व।
english: But the relation of own and owner: continuance of enjoyment of the properties of those whose regions are destroyed, according to each one's own.
notes: Verbless. ucchinna-deśānām could instead qualify dravyāṇām (properties of ruined regions). bhoga = enjoyment, use.

words.gram: n. acc. sg., pres. part. pass. √bhuj

words.gloss: from child, aged, sick, afflicted, absent, leaving the region, upheaval of the kingdom

hindi: जो अपना द्रव्य दूसरों द्वारा भोगा जाता हुआ दस वर्ष तक उपेक्षित करे, उसका ह्रास हो जाए, बालक, वृद्ध, रोगी, व्यसन वाले, प्रवासी, देश-त्याग और राज्य-विप्लव को छोड़कर।
english: Whatever own property, [while] being enjoyed by others, one disregards for ten years, would be lost to him, except in [the cases of] child, aged, sick, afflicted, absent, leaving the region and upheaval of the kingdom.
notes: vyasani is rendered 'afflicted' (calamity, vyasana); the alternative 'given to vice' (glossary 4.6) is possible. proṣita = gone abroad, absent. The exceptions are a dvandva list of persons and events, rendered as bare words.

hindi: बीस वर्ष से उपेक्षित और अनवसित वास्तु के विषय में पूछताछ न करे।
english: [One] should not question a site neglected for twenty years and unsettled.
notes: anavasita is obscure ('not settled', perhaps 'uninhabited' or 'not completed'); rendered 'unsettled'. anuyuñjīta = question (glossary 4.7).

words.gram: m. nom. pl., pres. part. vi-√vas

words.gloss: property of the king and the śrotriyas

hindi: ज्ञाति, श्रोत्रिय या पाषण्ड राजाओं की अनुपस्थिति में दूसरों के वास्तुओं पर रहते हुए उपभोग से न हरें: उपनिधि, आधि, निधि, निक्षेप, स्त्री, सीमा और राजा और श्रोत्रियों के द्रव्यों को।
english: Kinsmen, śrotriyas or pāṣaṇḍas, dwelling on others' sites in the absence of kings, should not take by enjoyment an upanidhi, a pledge, a treasure, a deposit, a woman, a boundary, and the property of the king and the śrotriyas.
notes: rājñām asannidhau 'in the absence of kings' is literal; the king(s) may rather be the owners meant. pāṣaṇḍa kept as a term (member of an order or sect). upanidhi and nikṣepa as in the glossary (4.6). 'hareyuḥ by bhoga' = take away by mere use.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., pres. part. ātm. a-√bādh

hindi: आश्रमी या पाषण्ड बड़े अवकाश में परस्पर बाधा न करते हुए रहें।
english: Members of orders or pāṣaṇḍas should dwell in a large space, not hindering one another.
notes: āśramin (one belonging to an āśrama) is rendered 'member of an order'. pāṣaṇḍa kept as a term, as in unit 32.

hindi: अल्प बाधा सहें।
english: [They] should bear a small hindrance.

hindi: अथवा पहले आया हुआ निवास की बारी दे।
english: Or the one who came earlier should give a turn of dwelling.
notes: paryāya = turn, rotation; the exact arrangement is not stated.

hindi: न देने वाला निकाल दिया जाए।
english: The non-giver would be expelled.

words.gloss: teacher, pupil, dharma-brother, one of the same tīrtha

hindi: वानप्रस्थों, यतियों और ब्रह्मचारियों के आचार्य, शिष्य, धर्मभ्राता और समान तीर्थ वाले क्रम से रिक्थ के भागी।
english: Of forest-dwellers, ascetics and students: teacher, pupil, dharma-brother and one of the same tīrtha [are] the sharers in the inheritance, in order.
notes: samāna-tīrthya is usually 'fellow-student' (one of the same tīrtha); rendered literally. The final -ā of tīrthyā is regular sandhi before r-. brahma-cārin rendered 'student'.

hindi: विवाद-पदों में और इनके जितने पण दण्ड हैं उतनी रातें राजा के क्षपण, अभिषेक, अग्निकार्य और महाकच्छ-वर्धन करें।
english: And in grounds of dispute, for as many nights as there are paṇas [of] penalties for these, they should perform the king's fastings, sprinklings, fire-duties and Mahakaccha-increasings.
notes: Obscure. The word division of the long compound is not certain; mahā-kaccha stays Mahakaccha (glossary 4.3). kṣapaṇa 'fasting', abhiṣeka 'sprinkling', agni-kārya 'fire-duty' are literal. Who 'they' are (the persons of units 32-33) and the sense of rājñaḥ ('of the king' or 'for the king') are not decided. Low confidence.

hindi: धन और सोने से रहित पाषण्ड साधु।
english: Pāṣaṇḍas without money and gold [are] good ones.

text_flags.why: likely typo: ḍh for ṇḍ (the word is printed pāṣaṇḍā in units 32 and 33)

notes: hiraṇya = money, suvarṇa = gold (glossary). Could also be read as 'the good ones among the pāṣaṇḍas are those without money and gold'. Verbless.

hindi: वे यथास्व उपवास और व्रतों से आराधना करें, पारुष्य, चोरी, साहस और संग्रहण को छोड़कर।
english: They should propitiate by fasts and vows, each according to his own, except in [the cases of] harshness, theft, rashness and seizing.
notes: The object of ārādhayeyuḥ is not stated. pāruṣya = harshness (verbal or physical injury elsewhere in Book 3); saṅgrahaṇa literally 'seizing' (in Book 3 the seizing of a woman), the sense is not imported here.

hindi: उनमें यथोक्त दण्ड करणीय।
english: In their case the penalties as stated are to be imposed.

hindi: राजा प्रव्रज्याओं में व्यर्थ आचारों को दण्ड से रोके। क्योंकि अधर्म से आहत और उपेक्षित धर्म शासक को मारता है।
english: The king should restrain by punishment vain practices in the renunciations. For dharma, struck by adharma and neglected, kills the ruler.
notes: pravrajyā = going forth into the wandering life, rendered 'renunciation'. vṛthā-ācāra may also mean 'those of vain conduct' (persons). śāstṛ is 'ruler, chastiser' (or 'teacher'); 'ruler' is taken from the context. The final verse of the chapter.
